question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2}$ of two pineapples is drawn from a population. The population has pineapples of two different weights, $1\,\text{kg}$ and $1.5\,\text{kg},$ distributed in the ratio $1:4.$ Calculate the standard error of $\overset{―}{X}.$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the pineapples in the population have weights $1\,\text{kg}$ and $\text{1.5}\,\text{kg},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $1:4.$ Therefore, to compute the population's mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $1+4=5$ pineapples only with the following weights:

$$
1\,\text{kg},\,1.5\,\text{kg},\,1.5\,\text{kg},\,1.5\,\text{kg},\,1.5\,\text{kg}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(1+4\cdot 1.5) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(1+6) \\  & =\frac{7}{5} \\  & =1.4\,\text{kg},\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{5}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}({1}^{2}+4\cdot {1.5}^{2})-{1.4}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(10)-1.96 \\  & =2-1.96 \\  & =0.04\,{\text{kg}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the sample size is $n=2,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}=\frac{0.04}{2}=0.02\,{\text{kg}}^{2}.
$$

Finally,

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{0.02}≈0.14\,\text{kg}.
$$
